mutations.label: a running resource with no machine on the runtime passes, which is #484 waved through by the gate built to stop it
mutations.find:
if [ "$status" = "absent" ]; then
      fail "$provider says $id is running, but no machine $name exists on the runtime (#484)"
    fi
mutations.replace:
if [ "$status" = "absent" ] && false; then
      fail "$provider says $id is running, but no machine $name exists on the runtime (#484)"
    fi

mutations.label: a machine the host holds Stopped answers for a resource the API calls running
a running resource that never recorded a machine passes in silence
mutations.find:
if [ -z "$name" ]; then
      fail "$provider says $id is running and recorded no machine for it — a claimed dataplane with nothing behind it (#484)"
    fi
mutations.replace:
if [ -z "$name" ] && false; then
      fail "$provider says $id is running and recorded no machine for it — a claimed dataplane with nothing behind it (#484)"
    fi

    fi
mutations.replace:
if [ -z "$acls" ] && false; then

mutations.replace:

mutations.label: a transport error reads as a seen witness: the reader that reported a live account empty for forty minutes, on this gate
mutations.find:
if ! doc="$("$read_instance" "$name")"; then
      fail "cannot look: reading machine $name off the runtime failed; no witness because nobody could look is not 'no witness'"
    fi
mutations.replace:
if ! doc="$("$read_instance" "$name")" && false; then
      fail "cannot look: reading machine $name off the runtime failed; no witness because nobody could look is not 'no witness'"
    fi

mutations.label: a balancer the runtime does not hold passes, which is #483 waved through by the gate built to stop it
mutations.find:
if [ -z "$found" ]; then
      fail "$provider registered balancer $wanted with a listener and a backend, and the runtime holds no balancer for it (#483)"
    fi
mutations.replace:
if [ -z "$found" ] && false; then
      fail "$provider registered balancer $wanted with a listener and a backend, and the runtime holds no balancer for it (#483)"
    fi

mutations.label: a balancer registered and holding nothing — no backend, no port — passes as delivered
every pack reads as claiming every capability, so the gate demands of Scaleway a balancer it never promised — the other half of #481
mutations.replace:
jq -e --arg p "$1" --arg c "$2" \
    '((.enforced[$c] // []) | index($p) != null) or true' >/dev/null

mutations.label: the machine reader matches by substring, so another run's machine answers for this one and the control stops biting
the rule-set reader loses the NIC filter key, finds nothing, and every firewall absence it reports is an instrument failure — the false #475
the balancer reader keys on a name pattern instead of the description the runtime writes, and reads zero on a host carrying one
the gate stops running the reader controls before it judges, so a broken reader files false absences again
mutations.replace:
true || witness_machine_reader_control
true || witness_acl_reader_control
true || witness_balancer_reader_control

note: The subject is #486: four issues in one evening (#475, #481, #483, #484) were four instances of one absent rule — a claimed dataplane needs a witness on the runtime, per provider. The verdicts live in witnesslib.sh so these mutations can neutralise each one and require the matching test to fail; the gate witness.sh is held by a structural test that these same mutations cover for the wiring. The two reader mutations are the ones worth reading twice: an ACL reader filtering on the wrong key reported 0 rule sets on a run carrying six during #486's own preparation, and filed as written that would have been a false #475 against Scaleway. The reader controls are what make that mistake fail the gate instead of the pack.
